comparator.academicYear: 2026–27 UvA curriculum and study guide, checked 2026-09-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum and one-page curriculum scheme establish a 60-EC first year. The first half of Year 2 contains 24 EC of taught courses, a 5-EC project and a 1-EC reflection practicum. In the second half, the published scheme places Regulatory Compliant Information Systems, Semantic Web and Recommender Systems concurrently before Research Methods for Interactive Systems and Applied Machine Learning; a 60-EC year permits two of the three concurrent 6-EC choices. This pathway selects the first two officially listed concurrent choices—Regulatory Compliant Information Systems and Semantic Web—then includes the two later courses, the 5-EC system project and 1-EC practicum. Year 3 similarly contains 30 EC genuine open choice, an 18-EC final project and a 12-EC selection from three listed 6-EC courses; this pathway selects the first two officially listed courses, Social Robotics and Logic and Society, rather than combining all three. The study guide confirms 180 EC, three years, Dutch, and full-time status.

alternatives.concept: Combines programming, databases, data science and computational methods with user-centred design, organisational change, research methods and responsible digital governance. It follows UvA's broad people-data-technology orientation while acknowledging that UCR lacks its dedicated semantic-web, regulatory-systems, social-robotics and compulsory project sequence.

alternatives.concept: Retains programming, databases, data science and organisational analysis but shifts the advanced programme toward perception, social psychology, interaction, language, institutional trust and technology adoption. It develops the explicit Human-Computer Interaction and Socio-Technical Systems directions as one coherent study of how people and institutions use and respond to digital systems.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest broad Information Science response is feasible. The official Data Science and Human-Computer Interaction directions each support a coherent additional curriculum with material course consequences, while Information Systems and Socio-Technical Systems are substantively represented in the closest core. All three included programmes pass the qualitative and pairwise 30-EC distinctness tests, so production stops at the permitted maximum of three.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Programming directly addresses the UvA programming component, with different scope and credits.
Introduction to Data Science directly addresses the UvA Data Science component and includes data visualisation, with different scope and credits.
Database Management Systems directly addresses the UvA modern-databases component, with different scope and credits.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics directly addresses the introductory logic component, with different scope and credits.
Machine Learning directly addresses the applied machine-learning component, with different scope and credits.
Linear Algebra addresses an important mathematical foundation within Mathematics for Information Studies, with different breadth and credits.
Computational & Numerical Methods addresses the computational modelling function of the UvA system-dynamics course, while using different models and credits.
UCR has no selected course equivalent to the disciplinary survey Keerpunten in de Informatiewetenschappen.
UCR has no selected dedicated Network Science course.
UCR data courses include visualisation, but no selected UCR course reproduces the dedicated Information Visualisation component.
UCR has no selected course that reproduces the information- and knowledge-management component.
UCR has no selected Semantic Web course.
UCR offers robotics only in the data-focused course pool and does not reproduce this selected compulsory Social Robotics component across the included programmes.
UCR has no selected course that reproduces the dedicated Logic and Society component.

Strategy & Digital Transformation addresses organisational analysis and responsible technology-driven change central to Regulatory Compliant Information Systems, with less legal and architectural depth.
Consumer Product Design directly contributes user-needs analysis and iterative design comparable to an important part of Interaction Design, while focusing on products more broadly.
Perception & Action directly addresses the perception side of the UvA cognition-and-perception component, with different disciplinary framing.
UCR design and strategy courses are related, but no selected course reproduces the UvA systems-oriented Modelling and Design component.
UCR has no selected dedicated Data Management and Governance Project.
Statistics & Experimental Methods addresses experimental and multivariate methods relevant to interactive-systems research, with different disciplinary scope.
The Art of Rhetorical Communication addresses the communication and presentation function of the UvA academic-skills practicum, while not being Information-Science-specific.
UCR does not reproduce this separate compulsory Information Science analysis project.

notes.text: The UvA programme integrates data science, information systems, human-computer interaction and socio-technical systems through dedicated modelling, design, governance, semantic-web, project and final-research components. UCR can combine substantial programming, databases, data analysis, user research, organisational change, cognition and responsible-technology study, but distributes them across computing, business, psychology, sociology, communication and philosophy rather than reproducing UvA's structured Information Science sequence.
